description: Drawing conclusions from samples with stated uncertainty: sampling distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, t-tests and ANOVA, chi-square tests for categorical data, linear regression with its assumptions checked, and non-parametric and resampling methods. Every procedure is first watched at work on thousands of simulated samples in the browser, then derived, then applied to real data such as district health records and market prices.
modelledOn: Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
Rice, Mathematical Statistics and Data Analysis
Efron and Hastie, Computer Age Statistical Inference
outcomes: Derive and simulate the sampling distributions of common statistics and explain the role of the central limit theorem.
Construct point estimators by the method of moments and maximum likelihood and compare them by bias, variance and mean squared error.
Build and interpret confidence intervals and carry out hypothesis tests, reporting p-values, effect sizes and power correctly.
Compare groups with t-tests, ANOVA and chi-square tests and choose the right test for the design and data type.
Fit linear regression models, check their assumptions with diagnostics and draw valid inferences from the coefficients.
Apply non-parametric tests, the bootstrap and permutation tests when parametric assumptions fail.

units.title: Populations, samples and sampling distributions
topics: Populations, parameters, samples and statistics; simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling; sampling frames and bias
Random variables refresher: expectation, variance, the normal, binomial, Poisson and exponential families
Sampling distribution of the mean and of a proportion; standard error; the law of large numbers
The central limit theorem stated, simulated and its limits with skewed data and small samples
Distributions derived from the normal: chi-square, Student's t and F; their shapes and degrees of freedom
Simulating thousands of household surveys in a Ghanaian district to watch estimates vary

units.title: Point estimation
topics: Estimators and estimates; bias, variance, mean squared error and consistency
Method of moments estimators
Maximum likelihood: the likelihood and log-likelihood, solving the score equation, numerical maximisation
Properties of maximum likelihood estimators: invariance, asymptotic normality, Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound
Sufficiency and efficiency in brief; Bayesian point estimates as a contrast

units.title: Interval estimation
topics: Confidence intervals: the pivotal method and what the confidence level does and does not mean
Intervals for a mean with known and unknown variance; intervals for a proportion (Wald, Wilson) and for a variance
Sample size calculation for a desired margin of error; finite population correction
Intervals for differences in means and proportions
Estimating malaria test positivity across district clinics with honest margins of error

units.title: Hypothesis testing
topics: Null and alternative hypotheses; test statistics, rejection regions and p-values; one- and two-sided tests
Type I and type II errors; significance level, power and power curves; sample size for a target power
The Neyman-Pearson lemma and likelihood ratio tests; the duality of tests and confidence intervals
Tests for a mean, a proportion and a variance; z and t tests
Multiple testing: family-wise error, Bonferroni and Holm corrections, false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg
Misuse of p-values, p-hacking and the replication crisis; reporting effect sizes and intervals instead of only significance

units.title: Comparing groups: t-tests and ANOVA
topics: Two-sample t-test with pooled and Welch variances; paired t-test; checking normality and equal variance
One-way analysis of variance: partitioning sums of squares, the F statistic and the ANOVA table
Post hoc comparisons: Tukey's HSD and planned contrasts
Two-way ANOVA with interaction; randomised block designs
Effect sizes: Cohen's d and eta squared; basics of experimental design and randomisation
Comparing maize yields across fertiliser treatments in a field trial

units.title: Categorical data and chi-square tests
topics: Contingency tables; joint, marginal and conditional proportions
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test; expected counts and the small-count rule
Chi-square test of independence and test of homogeneity; standardised residuals
Fisher's exact test; McNemar's test for paired proportions
Measures of association: relative risk, odds ratio and their confidence intervals; Simpson's paradox

units.title: Linear regression and its assumptions
topics: Correlation and simple linear regression by least squares; the regression line and R squared
Inference for slope and intercept; confidence intervals for the mean response and prediction intervals
Multiple regression in matrix form; categorical predictors and interactions; the overall F test
Assumptions and diagnostics: linearity, independence, constant variance, normal errors; residual and Q-Q plots
Leverage, influence and Cook's distance; multicollinearity and variance inflation factors; transformations
Correlation versus causation; confounding and omitted variables
Modelling tomato prices at Kumasi Central Market against season, rainfall and transport cost

units.title: Non-parametric and resampling methods
topics: Rank-based tests: sign test, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis
Spearman's rank correlation; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
The bootstrap: resampling, bootstrap standard errors, percentile and BCa confidence intervals
Permutation tests for group differences and correlation
When resampling fails: dependence, very small samples and extreme statistics

units.title: Inference in practice
topics: Choosing a method: a decision guide by question, design and data type
Frequentist and Bayesian inference compared: prior, posterior and credible intervals in brief
Survey data in practice: weights, non-response and design effects
Reproducible analysis and honest reporting; preregistration
Capstone: a full inferential analysis of a public Ghanaian dataset with a written report

schedule.title: Sampling and sampling distributions
schedule.exercise: Compare simple random and cluster sampling for a district household survey, listing what bias each could introduce through the sampling frame.

tasks.title: Draw simple random and stratified samples from a population table of 500 households and compare their mean income with the true mean
Simulate the sampling distribution of the mean for samples of size 5, 30 and 100 and verify that the standard error shrinks as predicted
Show how a biased sampling frame shifts survey estimates by simulating sampling from only households near a main road

schedule.title: Central limit theorem and derived distributions
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph when the central limit theorem works poorly, using skewed data with a small sample as the example.

tasks.title: Plot the sampling distribution of the mean for a skewed population at several sample sizes and note when it looks normal
Plot chi-square, t and F densities for several degrees of freedom and read off the critical values used for a 5 percent test
Simulate 5000 household surveys in a district, record each estimate, and report the spread of the estimates and the coverage of the true value

schedule.title: Point estimation
schedule.exercise: Derive the maximum likelihood estimator for the rate of a Poisson variable and compare it with the method of moments.

tasks.title: Find method of moments estimators for the mean and variance of a normal sample and check them on a data set of 30 values
Write the log-likelihood of an exponential sample, maximise it numerically, and compare the estimate with the analytic one
Check the asymptotic normality of a maximum likelihood estimator and the Cramer-Rao bound by simulation across several sample sizes

schedule.title: Confidence intervals
schedule.exercise: Explain to a district health officer what a 95 percent confidence interval does and does not mean, using a repeated-sampling picture.

tasks.title: Compute a 95 percent confidence interval for a mean with unknown variance from a sample of 25 values using the t distribution
Compare Wald and Wilson intervals for a proportion at several sample sizes and report their actual coverage by simulation
Estimate malaria test positivity at ten clinics with confidence intervals, adjust for different sample sizes, and decide which clinics truly differ

schedule.title: Hypothesis testing basics
schedule.exercise: Work out the power of a one-sided z test by hand for three effect sizes and describe how sample size changes the answer.

tasks.title: Carry out a one-sided z test on a sample mean, state the rejection region, and compute the p-value
Draw a power curve for a t test with three sample sizes and find the sample size that gives 80 percent power for a given effect
Construct the likelihood ratio test for a normal mean and show its link to the confidence interval for the same data

schedule.title: Standard tests and multiple testing
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on how p-hacking arises, with a numeric example of testing twenty outcomes and reporting only the one that is significant.

tasks.title: Perform z and t tests for a mean, a proportion and a variance on given samples and state each conclusion in plain words
Run 100 tests on pure noise, count the false positives, and then apply Bonferroni, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections
Simulate p-hacking by testing many subgroups, measure the rate of false discoveries, and show how preregistration changes it

schedule.title: Two samples and ANOVA
schedule.exercise: Choose the right test for five study designs and explain the assumptions you would check for each.

tasks.title: Run a Welch two-sample t test and a paired t test on given data, and check normality with a Q-Q plot
Build a one-way ANOVA table by hand from group totals and confirm the F statistic and its p-value
Follow a significant ANOVA with Tukey's HSD, find which treatment pairs differ, and report effect sizes with intervals

schedule.title: Designed experiments
schedule.exercise: Design a randomised block experiment for comparing three seed varieties on four farms, and explain how blocking improves precision.

tasks.title: Compute Cohen's d and eta squared for given group data and describe the size of each effect
Analyse a two-way ANOVA with interaction on a crop data set and interpret an interaction plot
Analyse maize yields across fertiliser treatments in a field trial, check assumptions, run post hoc tests and write the conclusions with intervals

schedule.title: Categorical data analysis
schedule.exercise: Compute expected counts and a chi-square statistic by hand for a two-by-two table, then check with software.

tasks.title: Test whether observed counts of births by day fit a uniform pattern with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test
Run a chi-square test of independence on a table of treatment and outcome, and inspect the standardised residuals
Compute relative risk and odds ratio with confidence intervals for a clinic data set, and demonstrate Simpson's paradox by stratifying

schedule.title: Regression
schedule.exercise: Interpret the coefficients of a fitted regression in plain words and state what the model cannot say about causes.

tasks.title: Fit a simple linear regression by least squares to 20 points, plot the line and report R squared
Compute confidence intervals for the slope and mean response and a prediction interval, and explain why the prediction interval is wider
Examine residual and Q-Q plots of a faulty model, find which assumption fails, and apply a transformation that fixes it

schedule.title: Diagnostics and market modelling
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page memo to a trader explaining which factors move tomato prices and which conclusions the data cannot support.

tasks.title: Compute leverage and Cook's distance for a small data set and identify the most influential point
Review a case that claims causation from a regression, list the confounders and omitted variables, and score the claim against a rubric
Model tomato prices at Kumasi Central Market against season, rainfall and transport cost, check multicollinearity, and report the best model

schedule.title: Non-parametric methods and resampling
schedule.exercise: Explain when a rank test is preferable to a t test and what you give up by using it.

tasks.title: Run a Wilcoxon signed-rank and a Mann-Whitney test on small skewed samples and compare their p-values with those of t tests
Compute bootstrap standard errors and percentile intervals for a median of 40 values using 5000 resamples
Show by simulation where the bootstrap fails for the maximum of a sample, and explain why with the sampling distribution

schedule.title: Choosing methods and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: state the question, design, methods, assumptions, results and limits of an analysis of a public Ghanaian dataset.

tasks.title: Choose the correct method for eight research questions using a decision guide, giving the design and data type that led to each choice
Compute weighted estimates and design effects for a survey with unequal selection probabilities and non-response, and compare them with unweighted ones
Carry out a complete inferential analysis of a public Ghanaian dataset with checks, interval estimates, multiple testing control and a reproducible script
